chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Verily God is more exalted and more noble than to be known through His creatures; rather, the creatures are known through God.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth.' I said: 'Whoever recognizes that he has a Lord, it is befitting for him to recognize that for that Lord there is pleasure and wrath, and that His pleasure and His wrath cannot be known except through revelation or a messenger.

So whoever does not receive revelation, it is befitting for him to seek the messengers, and when he meets them he recognizes that they are the Divine Authority and that obedience to them is obligatory.' And I said to the people: 'Do you know that the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) was the Divine Authority from God over His creatures?' They said: 'Yes.' I said: 'So when the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) passed away, who was the Divine Authority over His creatures?' So they said: 'The Quran.'

So I looked into the Quran and found that the Murji'ite, and the Qadariyya, and the atheist who does not believe in it all dispute using it, to the point of overpowering men through argumentation. So I recognized that the Quran cannot serve as a Divine Authority except with a custodian, and whatever he says concerning it would be true. So I said to them: 'Who is the custodian of the Quran?' They said: 'Ibn Mas'ud had some knowledge, and Umar had some knowledge, and Hudhayfa had some knowledge.' I said: 'All of it?' They said: 'No.'

So I found no one who could be said to know all of it except Ali (peace be upon him). And when a matter arose among the people, this one said 'I don't know', and this one said 'I don't know', and this one said 'I don't know', but this one said 'I do know.' So I testify that Ali (peace be upon him) was the custodian of the Quran, and obedience to him was obligatory, and he was the Divine Authority over the people after the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family),
and that whatever he said regarding the Quran is the truth.' So he (the Imam) said: 'May God have mercy on you.'

key_terms.الزِّنْدِيق: Atheist/Zindiq — in early Islamic usage, a materialist or crypto-dualist who denies revelation
key_terms.الطَّاعَة الْمُفْتَرَضَة: Obligatory obedience — obedience that is divinely mandated
key_terms.الْحُجَّة: Divine Authority/Proof (hujja) — the authoritative representative of God on earth, who constitutes a binding proof upon humankind
key_terms.الْقَدَرِيّ: Qadariyya — early theological group who affirmed absolute human free will
key_terms.الْمُرْجِئ: Murji'ite — member of an early Islamic theological school who deferred judgment on sinners
key_terms.قَيِّم: Custodian/guardian — one who stands over, maintains, and authoritatively interprets the Quran

ai.seo_question: Why did Mansur ibn Hazim argue that the Quran alone is insufficient as a Divine Authority without an Imam?
ai.summary: Mansur ibn Hazim, a trusted companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recounts to the Imam a rational argument he used to establish the necessity of a living Divine Authority (hujja) after the Prophet. He begins from the premise that God's pleasure and wrath can only be known through revelation or a messenger, then demonstrates that the Quran alone cannot serve as an authority without a qualified interpreter. Through dialogue with his contemporaries, he eliminates all candidates until only Imam Ali (AS) remains as the one who possesses complete knowledge of the Quran. The Imam endorses his reasoning with the supplication 'May God have mercy on you' — a characteristic expression of deep approval in early Shia discourse.
